candidate.answerReason: The common multiples of 4 and 5 up to 100 are 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100. Only 60 is also divisible by 3, and divisibility by 4 already ensures divisibility by 2.

methods.label: List the common multiples in range
methods.explanation:
A number divisible by \(4\) is already divisible by \(2\), so we only need to impose divisibility by \(3,4,5\). The least common multiple of \(4\) and \(5\) is \(20\). Hence their common multiples among the first hundred positive integers are exactly
\[
20,40,60,80,100.
\]
Only \(60\) is also divisible by \(3\). Thus exactly \(1\) integer satisfies all four divisibility conditions, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Finding common multiples and checking a list of five integers uses elementary arithmetic.
